propositions: Ticket directory creation with os.makedirs happens outside the write lock, leaving a window where the directory exists but its CREATE event file has not yet been written, which interruption (kill, timeout, host sleep) leaves behind empty stray ticket dirs that fsck reports as MISSING_CREATE and FOREIGN_STORE_PATH.

New staging.py module stages directory and first event together in a dot-prefixed temporary path (.tmp-newticket-{pid}-{uuid4hex}), then atomically publishes both with a single os.rename under the existing write lock, making temp paths invisible to fsck scanners without detector changes.

batch_stage_and_commit and inbound_translate._write_event_file and dispatch_one BRIDGE_ALERT emission shared the same dir-then-first-file vulnerability signature and are converted to use StagedEvent.promote() to close the interruption window.

sweep_stale_staging() removes only .tmp-newticket-* directories provably owned by dead processes using the write lock's v2 stamp (host + pid-namespace + start-time), bounded and best-effort, never touching ticket directories or event store data.
